column1: # Wire, connector, crimp-tool and heat-shrink BOM. Fills the gap identified when checking the controller BOM for completeness: control-system-bom.csv and part-numbers.csv cover ICs/modules/sensors/actuators but carried no wire/connector/tool line items at all. Sized against the actual branch currents already established elsewhere in this directory (control-system-bom.csv, module-interconnect.csv): heater branches ~5.4A continuous when firing AND physically near a heatsinked SSR dissipating 5-6W (ambient near that run is warm, ordinary PVC insulation is not appropriate); pump/valve branches are mA-level actual current but still need mains-rated insulation; the mains trunk from the IEC inlet through the T10A fuse must be rated at or above the fuse rating for the fuse to protect the wire that matters; 5V DC distribution is ~450mA measured against a 1A design max; signal wiring (GPIO/UART/I2C/SPI) is <20mA per line and gauge there is about handling/solderability, not current. AU-sourced to match this project's existing supplier pattern (Jaycar/Altronics/Core Electronics/element14 AU/RS AU, AliExpress only where nothing local exists).

column2: Jaycar WH3009 - Light Duty Hook-up Wire Pack 8 colours
column6: 26AWG (13/0.12mm) 0.6A-rated - current headroom is irrelevant here (<20mA/line), the gauge is chosen for handling and solderability on perfboard. 8 colours useful for tracing ~40+ connections

column1: 5V DC distribution wire (PSU to board / relay coils / dimmer logic)
column6: ~450mA measured against 1A design max - 22AWG gives comfortable margin. Landing method (screw terminal or crimp) is a build-time choice, not a wire-spec question

column2: IWISS SN-28B ratcheting crimper + connector/housing kit
column3: AliExpress / Amazon AU (no AU bricks-and-mortar stocks a bundled kit)
column6: MUST be the ratcheting SN-28B, not the flat pliers-style knockoff sold under the same name - check listings explicitly say 'ratchet'. Covers 28-18AWG at 2.54mm/3.96mm pitch (DuPont and JST-XH). Core Electronics stocks genuine Pololu 2.54mm housings/pins locally (POLOLU-1900) if a partial-local-sourcing split is preferred over one AliExpress order

column2: Jaycar WB1562 - Flexible Three Core Mains Cable
column6: 3-core (Active/Neutral/Earth), 250VAC 10A-class round PVC flex. Fine for pump/valve branches where actual current is mA-level but insulation rating still matters

column1: Mains trunk - inlet to fuse to distribution (must match T10A fuse rating)
column2: Jaycar WB1565 - Mains 10A Twin and Earth Power Cable
column6: 1.0mm2, 250VAC, 10A - matches the T10A slow-blow fuse rating so the fuse actually protects the conductor. WB1568 (20A/2mm2) is a fine upgrade if extra margin is wanted and cheap enough to justify

column1: Heater branch wire (~5.4A continuous, near heatsinked SSR - HIGH TEMP REQUIRED)
column2: Core Electronics FIT0584 - 16AWG (1.5mm2) High-Temperature Silicone Wire
column6: -60C to +200C silicone, tinned copper, correctly gauged and rated for the load next to the SSR heatsink's 5-6W dissipation. DO NOT substitute Jaycar WH3037 ('7.5A Heavy Duty Silicone') - it is 180C but only ~0.75mm2/18AWG and Jaycar itself rates it at only 7.5A, too close to the 5.4A continuous load for comfort next to a hot SSR. DO NOT substitute Altronics W2291 ('high temperature hook up cable') - despite the name it is only 105C-rated PVC, not silicone/PTFE, and does not meet the requirement. FIT0583 (14AWG/2.5mm2) is the step-up if more thermal/current margin is wanted

column2: Jaycar TH1829 - Heavy Duty Ratchet Crimping Tool for Insulated Terminals
column6: Genuine ratcheting mechanism (will not release until full crimp) - not the cheap pliers-style tool. 0.5-6.0mm2 range, colour-keyed jaws (red/blue/yellow). Alt: Altronics T2177 Crimptool Ratchet Multi-Connector Universal Kit

column2: Jaycar PT4530 - Quick Connect Crimp Connector Pack (160pc)
column6: 6.35mm/4.8mm/3.3mm quick-disconnect spades plus assorted ring/butt types, colour-keyed to TH1829's jaws. Match barrel colour to gauge: red = 0.5-1.5mm2 (covers the 0.75mm2 pump/valve branches), blue = 1.5-2.5mm2 (covers the 1.0-1.5mm2 heater/trunk branches) - do not crimp a 1.5mm2 conductor in a red barrel or a 0.75mm2 conductor loose in a blue one

column1: Heat shrink - general low-voltage strain relief
column2: Jaycar WH5525 - Assorted Heatshrink Pack 1.5-10mm (or WH5520 Ultimate Heatshrink Pack)
column6: Standard 2:1 polyolefin assortment - fine for perfboard/DuPont-side strain relief. NOT rated or intended for mains joints - see next row

column2: RS PRO Adhesive Lined Heat Shrink Tube 3:1 ratio
column3: RS Australia (also element14 AU under 3M/Pro Power/Raychem ATUM)
column6: 6.4/9/12.7mm diameters, ~1.2m lengths, MIL-DTL-23053/4 Class 3 / UL224, 125C / 600V - comfortably covers the 300V+ mains-joint requirement. Jaycar's own glue-lined heatshrink (WH5643, 4:1) is a lower-ratio water/dust-resistant product only, not explicitly voltage-rated - use it for low-voltage sealing, not mains joints

column2: Wago 221-412 (2-way lever connector) + 221-500 DIN mounting carrier
column3: Cutter Electronics / element14 AU / K&A Electronics
column6: 32A/450V per Wago datasheet WHEN mounted in the 221-500 carrier per spacing; free-hanging/unspaced the safe figure is closer to 275V - still well over the 240V/10A need either way, but MUST be seated in the carrier for proper strain relief and mechanical fixing, not left loose. Tool-less, fast, reusable, good with fine-strand appliance flex. Genuine Wago carries ENEC/VDE/UL/CSA approval, recognised under AS/NZS 3000:2018

column1: Mains distribution / daisy-chain - DIN rail terminal block option (RECOMMENDED for the permanent distribution point)
column2: Dinkle DIN rail terminal blocks (+ end clamp/end cap)
column3: Altronics (dinkle range) / Weidmuller or Phoenix Contact via element14 AU
column6: Standard UL-approved panel-building practice - positive mechanical DIN-rail mounting gives materially better vibration resistance than a free-floating lever connector (relevant here: pump vibration, thermal cycling from the SSR), clear per-terminal marking for inspection, screw clamp gives visible/tactile torque confirmation, easily isolated per-circuit for fault-finding. Needs the DIN rail itself mounted in the enclosure and periodic re-torque check on stranded conductors. This is the more standard/inspectable choice for the PERMANENT mains distribution point given this build's existing servicing-isolation theme; Wago 221s (above) are a legitimate faster-to-build alternative

column1: Mains joints - twist + tape / twist + heatshrink [NOT ACCEPTABLE - do not use]
column6: NOT acceptable practice for a permanent appliance mains joint. No listed/tested approval for the purpose (unlike Wago 221 or a proper terminal block - no AS/NZS 60998-type approval as a connector). Relies on friction/twist geometry not rated for vibration + thermal cycling. Heat shrink over a twist provides insulation only, not mechanical retention - contact pressure is not maintained as copper cold-flows/relaxes over time, no strain relief, and the joint is not inspectable without destroying the sleeve. Wire nuts are a fixed-building-wiring fitting (undisturbed, in a wall cavity), not an appliance-internal fitting subject to pump vibration and SSR thermal cycling. Use the Wago/DIN-terminal-block rows above, OR the genuinely-crimped closed-end connector row below, for every permanent mains joint in this build instead

column1: Mains joints - crimped closed-end connector [ACCEPTABLE for permanent non-serviceable splices only]
column2: RS PRO Insulated Closed End Connector, 1.25mm2 (22-16AWG) and 1.5-2.5mm2 (16-14AWG) ranges; also TE Connectivity/AMP 321-series End Splice, 300V rated
column4: varies - verify current AU stock/price at checkout
column5: medium - part numbers traced to manufacturer catalogue but live AU stock/price not confirmed
column6: THIS is what an OEM 'twisted and crimped' joint actually is - NOT the same as the twist+tape row above. A closed-end connector is a barrel closed at one end; all conductors enter the open end, get twisted together, and a SINGLE crimp compresses the whole bundle into a gas-tight metal-to-metal joint (the crimp plastically cold-flows the copper - this is why it needs no service access and is trusted in automotive/aerospace harnesses with zero rework). Do NOT search 'B-connector' at AU retailers - that term surfaces Jaycar's HP1214/HP1270/HP1272, which are gel-filled insulation-piercing LOW-VOLTAGE telecom/alarm splices, not mains-rated and the wrong product. Crimped with the SAME indent/oval jaw as the insulated butt-splice profile already on the Jaycar TH1829 ratchet crimper above - no new tool is strictly required, BUT multi-wire (3-4 conductor) caps have a fatter barrel than a 2-wire splice in the same colour class, so physically check the connector's rated barrel diameter against the TH1829's jaw opening before trusting a real joint - a cosmetically-closed crimp that didn't fully seat is not gas-tight. A dedicated RS PRO multi-cavity closed-end ratchet crimper exists as a fallback if the TH1829 doesn't fit. SERVICEABILITY CAVEAT: this joint is destructive to undo, same as any crimp terminal - use it ONLY for joints genuinely permanent and buried in the harness (matching the OEM precedent). Anything that might need rework during debugging keeps using the Wago/DIN-terminal-block rows above instead
